config.purpose: Diagnose foreground harm in the stopped equal-frame probability-memory baseline; this is not a new fusion variant or deployment experiment.
config.selection: The same eight independent_dev_added development logs, 321 keyframes; new holdout remains closed.
config.controls: One fresh PTv3 forward shared by the unchanged raw, current-spatial probability, previous-raw probability and hard-vote controls. Compare all control confusion matrices with the archived run, and explicitly report any non-reproduction.
privileged_diagnostics: Delete only historical neighbors with a different GT semantic class.
Additionally require the same nonzero GT instance for thing classes; unknown IDs cannot match. Stuff uses the class filter.
config.invariants: Same preceding raw scan, four neighbors, 0.25 m radius, 0.75 s expiry, supplied ego poses and 50/50 per-frame probability mixture. Never replace historical predictions with GT; never write a corrected output back. No motion correction, parameter search, training, model changes or holdout opening.
config.attribution: Report original fixes/harms, all-neighbors-same-class/instance harms, harms removed and introduced by each GT filter, per-class and per-object counts, for all points and camera foreground separately. Also measure online-only confidence, entropy, disagreement and distance distributions conditioned on evaluation outcomes; these are diagnostics, not chosen gates.
config.decision: If harms persist with all neighbors belonging to the right class/instance, correspondence alone is insufficient and evidence quality/readout needs attention. If GT filtering removes foreground damage, association is a plausible next target, not yet a deployable solution. Do not loosen the previous gates or report privileged scores as algorithm gains.
config.timing: Diagnostic observer recomputes neighbors and reads GT. Its wall time is not deployable latency. No probability caches or duplicate dataset are stored.
